title: Crown and Hollow
premise: Silas Joubert, a mercenary bound to the silent god Veth and keeper of ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors who believe prophecy is treason, she learns that the vanished country of Aurelle still exists behind a door only memory can open—and that the thirteenth turn of the moon will seal it forever. Betrayed by her guildmaster, who wrote the prophecy himself to buy his own survival, Silas must choose between loyalty to the people who raised her and the truth that will unmake them. In the end she opens the door, lets Aurelle finally die so its survivors can live free of it, and pays the price: every memory of the god she served.
about_author: W. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the private papers of defunct trading companies before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, gods, and the people who keep both running.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A night of routine work at the Guild—appraising a bottled storm, balancing accounts—establishes her meticulous invisibility and her habit of speaking prayers to a god that never answers. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Cataloguing an estate sale, she finds a prophecy book written a century ago; tonight's date and her full name appear in it, ending mid-sentence. She steals the page. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: Silas brings the page to guildmaster Corvane Hale, who goes pale and orders it burned—and orders her watched. Her friend and fellow ledger-keeper Maren covers for her. Emotional beat: first crack in trust.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Dessa Rook's POV. Rook, who hunts prophetic sedition for the Crown, receives an anonymous tip about the Guild. She is brilliant, weary, and genuinely believes prophecy killed her sister. Emotional beat: sympathy for the coming antagonist.

chapters.title: A Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Researching Aurelle, erased from maps after a war no one will discuss, she finds the prophecy describes a door 'that opens on remembering.' An old client, the cartographer Ivet, admits he has drawn roads to places he's never been. Emotional beat: dread mixed with wonder.

chapters.title: The God Who Went Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Silas's POV. Fifteen years earlier: how a starving orphan swore herself to Veth in exchange for survival, and how the god answered—once. Emotional beat: grief for the one voice that ever chose her.

chapters.title: Ledgers Do Not Lie
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren discovers entries in the Guild's oldest ledger in Corvane's hand, dated before they were written—the prophecy transcribed as accounting. She hides the discovery from Silas, torn between loyalty and truth. Emotional beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ivet agrees to guide her but demands she erase his name from the Guild's debt-book first—a small impossible thing. Rook raids the estate sale house hours behind her. Emotional beat: the hunt tightening.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook questions Maren, who gives nothing away but reveals enough. Rook realizes the Guild isn't selling prophecies—it's fulfilling one. Emotional beat: the hunter reframing the quarry.

chapters.title: Roads Drawn From Memory
chapters.summary: Silas and Ivet travel toward where Aurelle should be, following roads only Ivet can see because he dreamed them. The landscape grows wrong: twelfth-hour shadows, birds flying backward. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Corvane's Confession
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He wrote the prophecy a century ago—or rather, a dying Veth dictated it through him as payment for a bargain meant to save the god. He has spent a hundred years arranging Silas's life to fit it. Emotional beat: monstrous love.

chapters.title: The Turn of the Eleventh Moon
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ambushed by Crown soldiers, Silas survives only when something answers her prayer for the first time in fifteen years—Veth, faint, dying, and afraid. Emotional beat: hope that feels like a trap.

chapters.title: What Maren Burned
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. To protect Silas, Maren burns the incriminating ledger pages and is caught by Rook. Offered her life for Silas's location, she refuses—but Rook reads the ashes anyway. Emotional beat: loyalty priced in blood.

chapters.title: The Door in the Hollow
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They reach the hollow where Aurelle stood. The door exists only in shared memory; Ivet cannot open it alone. Silas remembers too much—she was born there, Corvane stole her out as an infant. Emotional beat: identity shattered and remade.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. Rook captures Ivet and offers Silas a trade: herself for the truth about Aurelle. Rook's certainty cracks when she sees evidence the Crown's founding war was itself a prophecy fulfilled. Emotional beat: the believer doubting.

chapters.title: The Price Written Down
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Corvane arrives with Guild enforcers; the prophecy requires Silas to enter the door at the thirteenth turn and never return, sealing Aurelle—and Veth—inside forever. He calls it salvation. She calls it a ledger entry. Emotional beat: confrontation with the author of her life.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Freed or escaped, Maren reaches the hollow and exposes Corvane's hundred-year manipulation to everyone—including that he silenced Veth deliberately to control the outcome. Enforcers waver. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon that cuts the wielder.

chapters.title: Twelfth Night
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Rook arrives not to arrest but to help—her sister's name is in the prophecy's margins too. Together they hold the hollow against Corvane's enforcers while the moon rises. Emotional beat: enemies becoming allies under pressure.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating brief beats. Silas opens the door with memory instead of blood, defying the prophecy's letter. Inside, the dying Veth asks her to stay and be its last keeper. She refuses—and offers it the one thing it never had: permission to end. Emotional beat: defiance as mercy.

chapters.title: What the Door Took
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Aurelle collapses into honest ruin; the survivors of its long stasis step out into a country that will grieve them. The price lands: Silas loses every memory of Veth, including the vow that made her. Emotional beat: hollow victory.

chapters.title: Balancing the Books
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Aftermath at the Guild: Corvane in chains of his own accounting, Rook burning her commission, Maren keeping the ledgers and adding one new line—Silas's debt, paid in full. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: A Woman With No God and Good Penmanship
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, epilogue. Memoryless but free, Silas takes honest work appraising ordinary things. On her desk, an old page in her own handwriting she doesn't remember writing: 'Remember me kindly.' She keeps it anyway. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
